title: Fastest Route Count
statement: A city has n intersections numbered 0 to n − 1 and two-way roads [a, b, minutes]. Return how many different routes from intersection 0 to intersection n − 1 take the shortest possible time, modulo 1,000,000,007.

answerKey.pattern: Dijkstra that also counts: ways[v] adds ways[u] on a tie and is replaced on an improvement
keyPoints: When a road gives a shorter time, set dist[v] and ways[v] = ways[u]
When it gives the same time, ways[v] += ways[u] (mod 1,000,000,007)
edgeCases: Many equal routes in a grid-like city
acceptableSlowerApproaches: Dijkstra, then a second pass over a DAG of tight edges: also O((n + m) log n)

hints: What extra number should each intersection carry besides its time?
How many fastest routes reach it.
In Dijkstra: shorter → copy the count; equal → add the count. Use 64-bit times.
